items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: Mill was his girl from a long time.

ctx.x: Absolutely. I wanted to ask you about Chicago. So this is early ‘30s? Mid-30s?

Mid. I left Chicago in ‘36. And probably I started with Duke in Detroit at the Fox Theater. And I was 18 and from Toronto. And of course Duke was Duke. And I was darned if I wasn’t going to go backstage. I didn’t know what backstage was all about, but I was going to go. So I did. And you know Duke had a marvelous sense of humor, and a marvelous feeling for life, so I knew it would be fun, interesting. And so when this gal appeared, you know, and sent up her — I sent him a letter on English note paper. Stanley and…

letter on the mirror? With all the fans he’d had, why was mine up there? And I looked at him and we looked at each other and I said, “I probably shouldn’t have forged it, should I?” And he said, “Oh I’m so pleased you did.” So we were friends forever after you know. That was wonderful. So he took me downstairs and said to the guys, “This is family, guys, lay off.” And it was wonderful, because I was family, and for the rest of my life, and for as long as he lived, I was family, and that was the greatest thing…
